memory_verse.label: Bible Portion
memory_verse.text: "Then ten of Joseph's brothers went down to buy grain from Egypt. But Jacob did not send Benjamin, Joseph's brother, with the others, because he was afraid that harm might come to him. So Israel's sons were among those who went to buy grain, for there was famine in the land of Canaan also" - Gen 42:3-5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Ten of the brothers set out for Egypt, but Jacob holds Benjamin back, "because he was afraid that harm might come to him." Benjamin was now the youngest, and the only remaining son of Jacob's beloved Rachel — the last living link, as Jacob believed, to the son he had lost. So the old favoritism continued: Benjamin was too precious to risk.

We can understand Jacob's fear. He had already lost, as he thought, one son of Rachel; he could not bear to lose the other. Grief and love made him protective. Yet we also see how a parent's fear, however understandable, can shape decisions in ways that reveal old patterns still at work. The favoritism that had once helped fracture this family had not fully died.

Fear has a way of gripping us long after a loss. It makes us cling tightly, hold back, and refuse to take risks, always bracing for the next blow. And while wise caution is good, fear that controls us can keep us from what God is doing.

Jacob's clinging fear would soon be tested, for the road ahead would require him to release even Benjamin. Sometimes God asks us to loosen our grip on what we hold most tightly, and to trust Him with what we fear to lose. Is there something you are gripping out of fear? Bring that fear to God, and learn to hold even your treasures with open hands.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Is fear from a past loss making you cling too tightly to something?
Are old patterns still shaping your decisions in ways you don't notice?
What do you need to hold with more open hands before God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, where fear from past losses makes me cling too tightly, help me to trust You. Teach me to hold even my treasures with open hands, knowing they are safest in Your care. Amen.
